title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of the member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: In 2020-2021, the Government in consultation with social partners continued to implement its first five-year National Action Plan on the Elimination of Child Labour (NAP) approved by Myanmar National Committee on the Elimination of Child Labour (MNCLEC) in December 2018. The plan has been well implemented across Myanmar with NAP structure that includes actions required from sub-national level State and Regional NAP committees. In December 2020, Factories and General Labour Laws Inspection Department disseminated the publication of the NAP to NAP- national committee members, and State and Regional level committee members, Child Labour Technical Working Group members and senior officers in different ministries. The Ministry of Labour, Immigration and Population planned to formalize the draft of the Hazardous Work List once the rule and regulations of the new Child Rights Law are finalized. On June 8 2020, the Government confirmed its commitment to addressing child labour by ratifying the Minimum Age Convention (ILO Convention 138). In October 2020, the Department of Social Welfare established a Nationwide Case Management Supervision Unit with a view to organizing a Government-led Case Management Mechanism and coordinating efforts on the protection and support of children and other target beneficiaries. The Case Management Task Force was re-structured with the participation of different stakeholders including ILO to ensure that child labour concern is mainstreamed in the national case management system. With the support of United States Department of Labor (USDOL), the ILO provided technical assistance to tripartite constituents to develop and initiate the implementation of its first National Action Plan (NAP) to eliminate child labour and its worst forms. ILO supported the consultations of national and subnational level NAP committees, and needs and gaps were identified to ensure the ILO demand-driven intervention. Training needs for committee members were responded by the ILO through an E-learning platform during COVID-19 pandemic. In compliance with UN engagement principles that affect the engagement with de facto Government, the ILO revised the beneficiaries for e-learning and targeted the Workers' and Employers' organizations and Civil Society Organizations. On yearly basis, the ILO in collaboration with tripartite constituents launched a comprehensive awareness campaign for World Day Against Child Labor through community level awareness activities, social media channels and photo exhibitions; generating awareness of child labor and the risk of COVID-19 increasing child labor. The ILO also assisted the publishing of NAP in both English and Myanmar Language as requested by Factory and General Labour Laws Inspection Department. To support the formalization of the hazardous work list, the ILO during the biennium supported the inclusive consultations of Technical Working Group on Child Labour and key stakeholders on strategy for adoption and enforcing the list. The ILO continuously advocated for ratification of ILO Convention-138, including providing clarification and running labour standards sessions for the constituents. Following Convention-138 ratification in June 2020, the ILO organized two webinars with key stakeholders on requirements of Convention No. 138 and Knowledge Sharing Webinar on Light Work. The ILO also provided technical support to Case Management Task Force under Nationwide case management system led by Department of Social Welfare.
